scope: analysis only, GEB main manuscript unchanged
motivation: Observed butterfly-resource climate-selective regional convergence could be a direct projection of known host plant floristic homogenization. Testing the identical climatic pattern alone has limited ecological novelty.
question: Is the climate-selective convergence of butterfly resource geography unusually strong for the ACTUAL exact butterfly-host network, relative to alternative exact-host assignments preserving butterfly diet composition at botanical-family level and plant usage degree?

network_null.operation: Bipartite double-edge swaps among host links whose plants belong to the SAME botanical family; swap (butterfly A, plant X) and (butterfly B, plant Y) to (A,Y),(B,X) only when new links absent
preserves: exact native and contemporary plant distributions in all regions
each butterfly's count of known host links in each botanical family
each plant species' number of butterfly consumers

primary.region_pairs: between WGSRPD Level1 continental codes and >=3000 km apart
primary.climate_distance: z(BIO1),z(BIO7),z(log1p(BIO12)),z(BIO15); Euclidean, frozen TTF independent climate crossfit
primary.analog: bottom quartile climate distance among eligible far pairs
primary.statistic: [mean Jaccard contemporary-native gain across climate analog far region pairs] - [mean Jaccard gain across climate discordant far region pairs], projected through butterfly-host links
primary.test: observed minus within-family host-link swap null median; one-sided Monte Carlo p<=0.05
primary.qualifiers: A positive result is conditional on exact host list quality and within-family rewiring, not direct evidence of butterfly use or interactions in each region.

stop_rule: If host identity null is not exceeded, treat the environmental selectivity as floristic structure inherited by butterfly resource projections and do not publish it as novel consumer-specific homogenization.
